faq.a: It depends on the night. For a steak dinner, locals point to Oak Steakhouse at Avalon or Cabernet Steakhouse on Windward. For Southern food, South City Kitchen and Smokejack lead the list. For something different, Rumi's Kitchen's Persian kabobs are a metro Atlanta favorite.

faq.q: Where should I eat at Avalon?
faq.a: Avalon's heavy hitters include Oak Steakhouse, South City Kitchen, Rumi's Kitchen, Colletta, Antico Pizza, Superica and The Cape's rooftop. Cafe Intermezzo is the move for dessert and late-night espresso.

faq.q: What restaurants are in Downtown Alpharetta?
faq.a: Downtown's Main Street area has Smokejack BBQ, The Southern Porch, Citizen Soul, Carson Kitchen, Hen Mother Cookhouse, Up On The Roof's rooftop brunch, Crust Pasta & Pizzeria and more, most within a short walk of the Town Green.

faq.q: Does Alpharetta have good brunch?
faq.a: Yes. Up On The Roof, Hen Mother Cookhouse and Carson Kitchen anchor downtown brunch, South City Kitchen and Superica run popular brunches at Avalon, and The Original Pancake House on Windward is the classic pancake stop.

faq.a: Alpharetta is home to hundreds of technology companies and a large share of metro Atlanta's top tech employers, supported by fiber infrastructure the city began investing in decades ago. Tech Alpharetta, the city's innovation arm, has run a startup incubator downtown since 2015.

faq.q: What are the main areas of Alpharetta?
faq.a: The best-known areas are Downtown Alpharetta around Main Street, Avalon on Old Milton Parkway, the Windward area to the north, the North Point corridor along GA 400, and Crabapple on the west side near Milton.

faq.q: What ZIP codes cover Alpharetta?

faq.q: How do people commute from Alpharetta?
faq.a: GA 400 is the spine of Alpharetta commuting, with exits 9 through 12 serving the city. Many residents work locally at the city's corporate campuses; others ride GA 400 south toward Sandy Springs, Buckhead and Midtown.

title: North Point Mall Redevelopment and NHL Arena in Alpharetta, GA: What's Planned (2026)
seoTitle: North Point Mall NHL Arena Plan in Alpharetta, GA (2026): Vote, Fulton Funding & What's Next
h1: North Point Mall Redevelopment and the Proposed NHL Arena: Where Things Stand
description: What's planned at North Point Mall in Alpharetta, GA: the 20,000-seat NHL-ready arena, apartments, hotels and offices, the 4-3 council vote, Fulton County's $192.4 million TAD deal and why it all depends on an NHL team.
coverPrompt: Photorealistic twilight aerial-style view of a large suburban shopping mall site being reimagined as a sports and entertainment district, a modern glass-and-steel hockey arena glowing in the foreground, mid-rise apartment and hotel towers, tree-lined walking paths and a green park, highway traffic light trails in the distance, warm charcoal and gold tones, no text, no logos, no readable signs, no recognizable real people

faq.q: Is North Point Mall closing?
faq.a: Not yet. The mall is still open and managed by Jamestown. Developers have said major demolition or construction is likely a year or more away, and the redevelopment only moves forward if the NHL awards a team to the site.

faq.q: Did Alpharetta approve the North Point NHL arena?
faq.a: Yes. Alpharetta City Council voted 4-3 at its Aug. 24, 2026 meeting to rezone the nearly 100-acre North Point Mall site for a plan that includes a 20,000-seat NHL-ready arena, apartments, hotels, offices and retail.

faq.q: Does Atlanta have an NHL team coming?
faq.a: No team has been awarded. The NHL has 32 teams and has said it is exploring expansion interest, with a Texas group described as further along than Atlanta or Arizona. Alpharetta's North Point plan and The Gathering at South Forsyth are both pursuing a team.

faq.q: What happens if Alpharetta doesn't get an NHL team?
faq.a: The approved plan does not happen. The city set an Aug. 24, 2031 deadline for an NHL team award, and developers have said they would need a new plan and new city approval without one.

faq.q: How is the North Point project being funded?
faq.a: Through the North Point tax allocation district, which sets aside future growth in property taxes inside the district for improvements there rather than creating a new tax. Fulton County approved up to $192.4 million in future tax revenue on Oct. 21, 2026, contingent on an NHL franchise.

h1: Alpharetta Retail Month 2026: Free Tote Bag Giveaway and Where to Shop Local
description: Spend $150 at local Alpharetta shops in November 2026 and get a free Shops of Alpharetta tote bag. Rules, excluded stores, Welcome Center hours and where to shop downtown, at Avalon, Windward and North Point.
coverPrompt: Photorealistic late autumn afternoon on a charming small-town brick sidewalk lined with boutique storefronts with plain solid-color awnings, three plain kraft paper shopping bags and a plain canvas tote bag resting on a wooden bench in the foreground, warm string lights and potted evergreens with small gold ornaments, soft golden-hour light, shallow depth of field, warm charcoal and gold tones, no text, no lettering, no logos, no readable signs, no people

faq.q: What is Alpharetta Retail Month?
faq.a: Retail Month is a November 2026 promotion from the Alpharetta Convention & Visitors Bureau that encourages shopping at local stores across four districts: downtown, Windward, Avalon and North Point. Shoppers who spend $150 or more at qualifying shops can get a free Shops of Alpharetta tote bag.

faq.q: How do I get the free Shops of Alpharetta tote bag?
faq.a: Spend $150 or more at eligible Alpharetta retailers between Nov. 1 and Nov. 30, 2026, then bring your receipts to the Alpharetta Welcome Center at 178 S. Main St., Suite 200. It's limited to one tote per household, while supplies last.

faq.q: Which stores don't count for the Retail Month tote bag?
faq.a: Receipts from Target, Costco, TJ Maxx, REI, Ross, HomeSense, Lowe's, Home Depot, Sam's Club, Walgreens, CVS and Best Buy are not eligible. Eligible purchases come from local shops and boutiques downtown, along North Main Street, at Avalon or inside North Point Mall.

faq.q: What are the Alpharetta Welcome Center hours?
faq.a: The Welcome Center is open Monday through Thursday from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. and Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. A virtual information kiosk is available Saturdays from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. The phone number is 678-297-2811.

faq.q: When is Small Business Saturday 2026?
faq.a: Small Business Saturday is Saturday, Nov. 28, 2026, the day after Black Friday. It falls inside Alpharetta's Retail Month.

title: Big Creek Greenway in Alpharetta, GA: Parking, Trailheads, Distances and Tips (2026)
seoTitle: Big Creek Greenway Alpharetta: Parking, Trailheads & Map (2026)
h1: Big Creek Greenway Guide: Where to Park, Best Stretches and Tips in Alpharetta
description: A local guide to the Big Creek Greenway in Alpharetta, GA: access points and parking, restrooms, the Rock Mill to Marconi route with mileage, trail rules and how it connects to Roswell, Forsyth and the Alpha Loop.
coverPrompt: Photorealistic wide paved greenway trail curving through a mature hardwood forest in late autumn, a short wooden boardwalk section crossing a gentle creek and marshy wetland, golden and amber leaves on the trees and scattered on the path, soft low golden-hour sunlight filtering through the canopy, a lone cyclist small and far in the distance seen from behind, warm charcoal and gold tones, shallow depth of field, no text, no lettering, no logos, no readable signs, no recognizable real people

faq.q: How long is the Big Creek Greenway in Alpharetta?
faq.a: The main Alpharetta section runs about 8 miles from Mansell Road and Big Creek Park north to Marconi Drive. Discover Georgia Outdoors lists it at 8.3 miles, Awesome Alpharetta says about 9 linear miles, and the city's Connected Alpharetta site counts 12 miles of Greenway trails in Alpharetta when spurs and connectors are included.

faq.q: Where is the best place to park for the Big Creek Greenway?
faq.a: Rock Mill Park on Kimball Bridge Road is a good first stop. It sits near the middle of the trail and has parking, restrooms and a pavilion. Other access points include Preston Ridge by the Alpharetta Family YMCA, Northpoint Park, Haynes Bridge Road, Marconi Drive and Union Hill Park. Beaver Creek Park is trail access only.

faq.q: Where are the restrooms on the Big Creek Greenway?
faq.a: Restrooms are at Rock Mill Park (the Kimball Bridge parking area), by the Alpharetta Family YMCA at Preston Ridge, and at the southern end of Big Creek Park in Roswell.

faq.q: Can you bike on the Big Creek Greenway?
faq.a: Yes. The 12-foot-wide paved path is open to cyclists, walkers, runners and skaters. Bikes are limited to 15 mph, and Greenway rules require cyclists and skaters to wear helmets.

faq.q: Does the Big Creek Greenway connect to Forsyth County?
faq.a: Forsyth County has its own section of the Big Creek Greenway that runs from McFarland Parkway north to Bethelview Road, with access at Fowler Park. The Alpharetta and Forsyth sections were built separately, with plans to link them over time.

title: Fulton County Schools Redistricting 2026: Draft Maps Would Combine Haynes Bridge and Holcomb Bridge Middle Schools
seoTitle: Fulton Schools Redistricting 2026: Haynes Bridge & Holcomb Bridge Draft Maps
h1: Fulton County Schools Redistricting: What the Draft Maps Mean for Alpharetta Families
description: Fulton County Schools' first draft maps for north Fulton would consolidate Haynes Bridge and Holcomb Bridge middle schools and shift some Barnwell-area students to Autrey Mill. Enrollment numbers, forum dates and the vote timeline.
coverPrompt: Photorealistic exterior of a generic suburban American public middle school building in late autumn, red brick and glass entrance with a covered walkway, an empty yellow school bus parked along the curb, golden and amber fall trees, a few scattered leaves on the sidewalk, soft late-afternoon golden-hour light, calm and quiet with no people, warm charcoal and gold tones, shallow depth of field, no text, no lettering, no logos, no readable signs, no recognizable real people

faq.q: Are Haynes Bridge and Holcomb Bridge middle schools closing?
faq.a: Not yet. Fulton County Schools' first draft map, released Nov. 8, 2026, would consolidate the two schools' students into a replacement middle school, with a preferred site next to the current Holcomb Bridge campus. It is only a draft. The district will revise it after community forums, and the school board's final vote is scheduled for Feb. 25, 2027.

faq.q: Which schools are part of the Fulton County Schools Region C redistricting?
faq.a: Four middle schools (Autrey Mill, Elkins Pointe, Haynes Bridge and Holcomb Bridge) and four elementary schools (Esther Jackson, Hembree Springs, Mimosa and Vickery Mill), all north of the Chattahoochee River.

faq.q: When are the Fulton County Schools redistricting forums?
faq.a: The draft map forums are Nov. 9, 2026 for elementary schools (6:30 to 8:30 p.m., Roswell High School gym) and Nov. 11 for middle schools (6 to 8 p.m., Centennial High School gym). Revised maps will be shown Dec. 14 (elementary) and Dec. 15 (middle) at the same places.

faq.q: How can I give feedback on the Fulton County Schools draft maps?
faq.a: Attend a forum, fill out the online survey the district posts the day after each forum, or email planning@fultonschools.org. You can also call the Operational Planning office at 470-254-5540.

faq.q: Why is Fulton County Schools redistricting north Fulton?
faq.a: Enrollment is falling. The district says many Region C buildings will stay underused through 2030-31. This year Haynes Bridge Middle is 57% full and Holcomb Bridge Middle is 53% full, based on the 20-day enrollment count.

description: Avalon on Ice opens Nov. 22, 2026 and runs through Jan. 18, 2027. Hours, holiday hours, $18/$14 ticket prices, waiver and reservation tips, plus what happened to The Cooler.

faq.q: When does Avalon on Ice open in 2026?
faq.a: Avalon on Ice opens Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026 (3 to 10 p.m. on opening day) and runs through Monday, Jan. 18, 2027.

faq.q: How much does Avalon on Ice cost?
faq.a: General admission is $18 per person and children 12 and under are $14. Skate rental is included in both prices.

faq.q: What are the Avalon on Ice hours?
faq.a: Regular hours are 3 to 9 p.m. Monday through Friday, 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. Saturday and noon to 7 p.m. Sunday. The rink is open 10 a.m. to 10 p.m. Nov. 23 to 27, Dec. 20 to Jan. 3, New Year's Eve and Day, and on all Fulton County public school holidays.

faq.q: Do I need a reservation for Avalon on Ice?
faq.a: Avalon recommends booking a time slot in advance. Walk-ups are welcome but not guaranteed a slot. Every skater, including walk-ups, must complete a waiver. Tickets are non-refundable and non-transferable, but you can reschedule if space is available.

faq.q: Is The Cooler in Alpharetta still open for ice skating?
faq.a: No. The Cooler's ice closed on March 31, 2025, and the building was converted into the Atlanta National Pickleball Club. Avalon's seasonal outdoor rink is now the main place to skate in Alpharetta.

faq.q: Did Alpharetta approve the North Point Mall arena?
faq.a: Yes. The Alpharetta City Council approved the zoning for the North Point Mall redevelopment 4-3 on August 25, 2026, with Mayor Jim Gilvin casting the deciding vote.

faq.q: Is an NHL team coming to Alpharetta?
faq.a: Not yet. The NHL has made no commitment to a team in metro Atlanta. A major part of the deal depends on the NHL committing to a team in Alpharetta by August 2031, and a rival arena project in Forsyth County is competing for the same team.

faq.q: How many apartments are in the North Point plan?
faq.a: Plans presented at a June 2026 town hall included 1,385 for-rent apartments, alongside a 20,000-seat arena, a music hall, two hotels, a conference center and 750,000 square feet of offices.

faq.q: Why did people oppose the North Point arena?
faq.a: Critics raised density, traffic, parking, possible taxpayer funding, hockey's track record in Atlanta and competition with Avalon and downtown. Supporters cited investment, a second life for a declining mall and national attention.

description: GA 400 toll lane construction began in April 2026. What Alpharetta commuters need to know: the flex lane closing Dec. 13, how dynamic tolls work, the 50-year private deal and the arguments on both sides.

faq.q: When will the GA 400 express lanes open?
faq.a: Construction began April 22, 2026 and is expected to take about five years, with completion expected in early 2031.

faq.q: Is the GA 400 flex lane closing?
faq.a: Yes. The northbound flex lane from just south of the Webb Bridge Road overpass to exit 11 (Windward Parkway) closes permanently starting December 13, 2026 for express lane construction. Four northbound lanes stay open.

faq.q: How much will the GA 400 tolls cost?
faq.a: Tolls will be dynamic, changing with real-time traffic. When speeds drop below 45 mph, the operator can raise rates, and the toll cap adjusts with Georgia economic data for growth and inflation. Exact prices have not been set.

faq.q: Who will run the GA 400 express lanes?
faq.a: A private company, SR 400 Peach Partners, will run the lanes. In exchange for 50 years of toll revenue, it funds construction and maintenance for the length of the contract.
